functions.description: Derive the annual declining-balance depreciation rate from the useful life and the method's acceleration factor.
inputs: the useful life of the asset expressed in years
the name of the declining-balance depreciation method to apply with its acceleration factor
outputs: annual depreciation rate as a fraction

functions.description: Compute one year of declining-balance depreciation from the beginning book value and annual rate, capped so the ending book value does not fall below the salvage value floor.
inputs: beginning book value for the year
annual depreciation rate as a fraction
the salvage value (residual value) of the asset at the end of its useful life with currency unit
outputs: ending book value for the year

functions.description: Run the year-by-year declining-balance schedule from the acquisition cost up to the target year and return the book value at the end of that year.
inputs: the original acquisition cost of the asset with currency unit
annual depreciation rate as a fraction
the salvage value (residual value) of the asset at the end of its useful life with currency unit
the target year number for which the end-of-year book value is requested
outputs: book value at end of target year from schedule

functions.description: Cross-check the scheduled book value against the closed-form expression cost times (1 - rate) raised to the target year, when the salvage floor is not reached.
inputs: the original acquisition cost of the asset with currency unit
annual depreciation rate as a fraction
the target year number for which the end-of-year book value is requested
book value at end of target year from schedule
the salvage value (residual value) of the asset at the end of its useful life with currency unit
outputs: closed-form book value agrees with schedule flag

functions.description: Compute the end-of-year book value of an asset under declining-balance depreciation with a salvage-value floor, rounded to cents.
inputs: the original acquisition cost of the asset with currency unit
the salvage value (residual value) of the asset at the end of its useful life with currency unit
the useful life of the asset expressed in years
the target year number for which the end-of-year book value is requested
the name of the declining-balance depreciation method to apply with its acceleration factor
outputs: end-of-year book value of the asset in dollars rounded to cents

entry_points.text: Equipment costs ●1, has a salvage value of ●2, and a useful life of ●3. Using ●5 depreciation, what is its book value at the end of year ●4?

params.description: the original acquisition cost of the asset with currency unit
params.validity_range: Must be a positive monetary amount, strictly greater than the salvage value so that depreciable base is positive; a zero or negative cost is logically invalid.

params.description: the salvage value (residual value) of the asset at the end of its useful life with currency unit
params.validity_range: Must be non-negative and strictly less than the acquisition cost; a salvage value equal to or above cost leaves no depreciable amount, and a negative salvage value is invalid.

params.description: the useful life of the asset expressed in years
params.validity_range: Must be a positive whole number of years, at least 2 for declining-balance rates (2/n) not to exceed 100 percent; a zero, negative, or fractional life is logically invalid for this schedule.

params.description: the target year number for which the end-of-year book value is requested
params.validity_range: Must be a positive integer; meaningful values run from 1 up to the useful life, and years beyond the useful life would simply return the salvage value by convention.

params.description: the name of the declining-balance depreciation method to apply with its acceleration factor
params.validity_range: Must be a declining-balance method with a positive acceleration factor (for example factor 2 for double-declining-balance, 1.5 for 150%); straight-line or units-of-production methods do not fit this template because they do not apply a rate to the beginning book value.
